headline_tiles: vocabulary collapse at equal proteins sampled

blocks.html: Erythroparvovirus is the only genus in the module. Six features are declared: NS1, the capsid pair VP1 and VP2, and three small proteins named for their mass — 7.5K, 9.5K and 11K.

rows: genomes in the BV-BRC protein dump

blocks.html: Four of the six carry copy_num: NS1, VP1, 7.5K and 9.5K. That two of the three accessory proteins are treated as essential is unusual in this family and is the measurement's doing, not a judgement — both are called in roughly 94% of the panel.

The 11 kDa protein is the one with a described function: a proline-rich protein that binds Grb2. The 7.5 and 9.5 kDa proteins cluster cleanly and are callable, and what they do is not established, so they are named uncharacterized lineage specific rather than given a function they have not been shown to have.

sections.lede: One genus, built around parvovirus B19 and its three small accessory proteins.
sections.title: What the module covers

rows: Replication initiator protein NS1 (HUH endonuclease and SF3 helicase)

blocks.html: Sixty-one distinct annotation strings collapse onto the six feature names. VP1 draws on eighteen, NS1 on sixteen, VP2 on thirteen. The 7.5 kDa protein comes from exactly one string across 171 deposits — a protein with no function to argue about also has no synonyms to collapse.

Three strings did not collapse, four sequences in all: NS2, initiator protein NS1 (EC 3.1.21.-) and hypothetical protein VP. The first of those is the interesting one: Erythroparvovirus is not described as encoding an NS2, and a single deposit under that name is not enough to declare a feature.

sections.lede: Profiles are built from the annotation strings BV-BRC already carries, after the strings are collapsed onto one name per protein.
sections.title: How it was built

blocks.html: The floors are 9.5K 102, 11K 116, 7.5K 149, VP1 300, VP2 359 and NS1 455 bits. Fifteen profiles in all, which is a small set for 1,721 source sequences — the genus is tight enough that five profiles cover all 307 NS1 deposits.
Self-recall is 307 of 307 for NS1, 275 of 275 for VP1, 143 of 143 for VP2, 53 of 53 for 11K, 17 of 17 for 7.5K and 21 of 22 for 9.5K. One miss in the whole module.

Self-recall against each feature's own in-range collection: 816 of 817 (99.9%) — NS1 307/307, 11K 53/53, 9.5K 21/22, 7.5K 17/17, VP 275/275, VP2 143/143. This is a floor, not a validation; the genome-level figures are in §05 and §06.

sections.lede: Each profile carries a bit-score floor and a length window taken from the collection it was built from.
sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit

rows: genomes ≥ 5 kb, clustered at 95% nucleotide identity

blocks.html: Routing was measured against the 14 reference contigs this module ships, of which 8 were used by the exemplar set.
All 30 exemplars routed, and all 30 routed to this module. Nothing went elsewhere and nothing was left unrouted.

That is the cleanest routing result in the family, and it follows from the genus being narrow: fourteen reference contigs are enough when the genomes they stand for are closely related to each other and to nothing else in Parvoviridae.

sections.lede: Routing is a BLASTn of the query against the reference contigs.
sections.title: Does it route?

blocks.html: 13 of 30 routed exemplars get every one of the 6 core features. Features trailing the best-called core protein by 20 points or more: 11k, 9.5k, 7.5k. 2 routed exemplar(s) cleared no profile at any feature and are counted here as calling nothing.
Across the 30 exemplars: VP1 27, VP2 27, NS1 25, 9.5K 17, 7.5K 16, 11K 13.

The accessory proteins look weak here and are not. The exemplar set is drawn to span the genus's diversity, so it over-represents the divergent isolates in which the small proteins are least recognisable; on the 300-genome panel 7.5K is missing in 17 genomes and 9.5K in 16, which is the 94% that justified marking them essential.

sections.lede: Calling is measured on the exemplars, feature by feature.
sections.title: Does it call the proteins?

blocks.html: The panel is 300 genomes drawn from the module's own sample; it is not held out. Genuinely clean means no genome, contig or feature flag at all.

blocks.html: 263 of 300 come through with no genome-level and no contig-level flag, and all 263 are genuinely clean — this module has almost no feature-level flags at all, eight in 300 genomes.

The flags that do appear are mostly not about the proteins: 19 genomes have a contig with more than 1% ambiguous bases. After those come 7.5K missing in 17, 9.5K missing in 16, VP1 missing in 5, NS1 missing in 5, VP1 called twice in 2.
Read the headline figure for what it is. The panel still contains the genomes the reference contigs were taken from, so it measures internal consistency, not out-of-sample behaviour.

sections.lede: The panel is 300 genomes drawn from the module's own sample; it is not held out.
sections.title: Are the calls right?

blocks.html: Two essential features are proteins nobody has characterised. A genome missing 7.5K or 9.5K is flagged, and 33 of 300 are. If a clade genuinely lacks one of them, this module will call that clade defective. The 0.85 rule that set copy_num measures how often a feature is called, not whether it ought to be there.

No splice features are declared. B19 transcription is heavily spliced, and the small proteins are made from spliced messages — but each is deposited as a protein often enough to cluster and be called by a profile, so the module calls the product without modelling the junction. A spliced product that was never deposited would be invisible here.
The single NS2 deposit is tracked, not resolved. It sits in UNASSIGNED_TRACKING.tsv with two other strings. That file is a list of unfinished work, not a resolution.

Use this module for erythroparvovirus genomes; routing and calling are both strong. Treat a missing 7.5K or 9.5K flag as a question about the genome's clade rather than as a defect, and check the ambiguous-base flag before blaming the module for anything.

sections.lede: Three limits, each measured rather than supposed.
sections.title: What it cannot do

blocks.html: The capsid labels were wrong on a large scale, and only applying copy_num exposed it. Before the capsid rebuild, 281 of 300 genomes had VP1 and VP2 called at identical coordinates — the two profiles were built from deposits that disagreed about which form they held, so both landed on the same open reading frame.

Rebinning the nested forms by size per species, rather than by the name on the deposit, and rebuilding the profiles took that from 281 of 300 to 1. The deposited name is a claim about which form a submitter thought they had; it is not a measurement.

blocks.html: Rarefaction over proteins: every annotated protein in the 112 genomes both sources annotate (396 source product records, 583 module calls) shuffled 100 times and drawn one at a time. Both curves start at zero. The source vocabulary reaches 43 distinct strings, the module's 6. At the depth both reach, 396 proteins, free text has used 43.0 strings against 6.0 — a 7.2-fold difference. The source reaches 95% of its final size after 332 proteins, the module after 26.

396 deposited protein strings across 112 genomes reduce to six feature names. The saturation curve on the companion page shows the deposited vocabulary still climbing with each genome added while the called vocabulary is flat at six.
Three strings resisted, four sequences in all.
